title: Characteristic Length of Meso-Structure as a Physical Fact for a Class of Brittle Materials
content: The recently-proposed nonlocal macro meso-scale consistent damage (NMMD) model has been applied successfully to various static and dynamic fracture problems. The characteristic length in NMMD model, though proved to be necessary for the mesh insensitivity of strain-softening regime, remains to be estimated indirectly with considerable arbitrariness. Such an issue also exists in other nonlocal models, e.g., peridynamics and phase field model. To overcome this obstacle, a series of dog-bone specimens made of polymethyl-methacrylate (PMMA) material with and without circular defect are investigated in this paper. It is found that NMMD model with the appropriate influence radius can correctly capture the experimentally-observed size effect of defect, which challenges the conventional local criteria without involving characteristic length. In addition to being directly measurable and identifiable in experiments, based on the two-scale mechanism of NMMD model, the characteristic length is also theoretically calibrated to be related to the ratio of fracture toughness to tensile strength of the material. Comparisons with the predictions of other modified nonlocalized criteria involving some kind of characteristic length demonstrate the superior ability of NMMD model to simulate brittle crack initiation and propagation from non-singular boundary. Revalidation of short bending beams demonstrates the theoretical calibration is also suitable for problems of mixed-mode fracture with stress singularity. Although limited to brittle materials like PMMA, the current work could be generalized to analysis of quasi-brittle even ductile fracture in the future.
